nodes.name: Select Un-judged Artifacts

parameters.query:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT 'extraction' AS artifact_type, l.lead_id AS artifact_ref, l.lead_id, l.business_id, l.trace_id,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'email', jsonb_build_object('from_name', l.raw_payload->>'from_name', 'from_email', l.from_email,
                                  'subject', l.subject, 'body', l.body),
      'extraction', jsonb_build_object('contact_name', e.contact_name, 'contact_email', e.contact_email,
        'company', e.company, 'budget_value', e.budget_value, 'budget_currency', e.budget_currency,
        'product_interest', e.product_interest, 'urgency', e.urgency, 'location', e.location)
    ) AS payload
  FROM vaibhavcapstone_leads l JOIN vaibhavcapstone_extractions e USING (lead_id)
  WHERE e.classification = 'ENQUIRY'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vaibhavcapstone_judge_scores j
                    WHERE j.artifact_type = 'extraction' AND j.artifact_ref = l.lead_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'draft', d.draft_id, d.lead_id, d.business_id, l.trace_id,
    jsonb_build_object('tone_instruction', b.config->>'tone',
      'allowed_products', COALESCE(r.items, '[]'::jsonb),
      'draft_subject', d.subject, 'draft_body', d.body)
  FROM vaibhavcapstone_drafts d
  JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l ON l.lead_id = d.lead_id
  JOIN vaibhavcapstone_businesses b ON b.business_id = d.business_id
  LEFT JOIN vaibhavcapstone_recommendations r ON r.lead_id = d.lead_id
  WHERE d.draft_type = 'CUSTOMER'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vaibhavcapstone_judge_scores j
                    WHERE j.artifact_type = 'draft' AND j.artifact_ref = d.draft_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'reasons', q.lead_id, q.lead_id, q.business_id, l.trace_id,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'extraction', jsonb_build_object('contact_name', e.contact_name, 'company', e.company,
        'budget_value', e.budget_value, 'product_interest', e.product_interest, 'urgency', e.urgency),
      'rubric_breakdown', q.reasons->'rubric', 'reasons', q.reasons->'reasons')
  FROM vaibhavcapstone_qualifications q JOIN vaibhavcapstone_extractions e USING (lead_id) JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l USING (lead_id)
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vaibhavcapstone_judge_scores j
                    WHERE j.artifact_type = 'reasons' AND j.artifact_ref = q.lead_id)
) x ORDER BY artifact_type LIMIT 15;

nodes.notes: Doer = Gemini, grader = OpenAI (different family - no self-preference). UNIQUE(artifact_type, artifact_ref) makes judging idempotent. 15 artifacts per sweep.

nodes.name: Persist Score + Telemetry

parameters.query:
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::text at, $2::text ref, $3::text lead, $4::text biz, $5::int score,
                  $6::jsonb viol, $7::text reasoning, $8::boolean ok,
                  $9::int lat, $10::int itok, $11::int otok, $12::numeric cost),
ins AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_judge_scores
  (business_id, lead_id, artifact_type, artifact_ref, judge_model, score, violations, reasoning)
  SELECT biz, lead, at, ref, 'gpt-4o', score, viol, reasoning FROM p WHERE ok
  ON CONFLICT (artifact_type, artifact_ref) DO NOTHING RETURNING score_id),
tel AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_llm_calls
  (business_id, lead_id, trace_id, call_site, prompt_version, model, latency_ms,
   input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, schema_valid, attempt, fallback_used, finish_reason)
  SELECT biz, lead, NULL, 'judge', 'v2', 'gpt-4o', lat, itok, otok, cost, ok, 1, false, NULL
  FROM p RETURNING call_id),
ev AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_events (business_id, lead_id, trace_id, agent, action, actor, detail)
  SELECT biz, lead, NULL, 'llm-judge', 'JUDGE_SCORED', 'system',
    jsonb_build_object('artifact_type', at, 'artifact_ref', ref, 'score', score, 'violations', viol)
  FROM p WHERE ok RETURNING event_id)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM ins) AS inserted, (SELECT score FROM p) AS score,
       (SELECT at FROM p) AS artifact_type, (SELECT ref FROM p) AS artifact_ref,
       (SELECT viol FROM p) AS violations, (SELECT biz FROM p) AS business_id;

nodes.name: Ship LF judge

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (() => { const v = $('Parse Verdict').item.json; const raw = $('OpenAI Judge').item.json; const u = raw.usage || {}; const now = new Date().toISOString(); const tid = v.trace_id || ('judge_' + v.artifact_ref); const uniq = tid + '-judge-' + Date.now(); return JSON.stringify({ batch: [{ id: uniq + '-t', timestamp: now, type: 'trace-create', body: { id: tid, name: 'lead-pipeline', metadata: { business_id: v.business_id } } },{ id: uniq + '-g', timestamp: now, type: 'generation-create', body: { id: uniq, traceId: tid, name: 'judge_' + v.artifact_type, model: 'gpt-4o', endTime: now, usage: { input: u.prompt_tokens || 0, output: u.completion_tokens || 0, unit: 'TOKENS' }, metadata: { artifact_type: v.artifact_type, artifact_ref: v.artifact_ref, business_id: v.business_id }, output: JSON.stringify({ score: v.score, violations: v.violations }).slice(0, 2000) } },{ id: uniq + '-s', timestamp: now, type: 'score-create', body: { id: uniq + '-sc', traceId: tid, name: 'judge_' + v.artifact_type, value: v.score == null ? 0 : v.score, comment: String(v.reasoning || '').slice(0, 500) } } ] }); })() }}

parameters.content:
## The AI that checks the AI

Every so often this picks up work the system has already done — facts pulled from an email, products recommended, replies drafted — and has a **different company's AI** grade it out of five.

The question it asks is narrow on purpose: **was anything invented?** Not "was this good", not "would I have phrased it differently". Only: is every claim actually supported by what was in front of it.

### Find work that hasn't been graded

**Every half hour**, or on demand for a demo.

**Pick up anything not yet graded.** Each piece of work is graded exactly once — and that's enforced by the database rather than by the workflow remembering, so a rerun can't quietly double-count anything.

**One at a time**, so one slow marking doesn't hold up the rest.

### Grade it — using a rival's model, deliberately

**Build the marking scheme** for whichever kind of work this is. The rules are strictest about one thing: **an empty field is never a fault.** Blank means the system declined to guess, which is exactly what it was told to do. Only a filled-in field can be wrong.

**Ask OpenAI's model to mark it.** Google's AI did the work, so OpenAI does the marking — a model never grades its own homework.

And unlike everywhere else in this system, the marker has **no backup model**. Falling back to Google here would defeat the entire point of asking someone else.

**Read the verdict** — a score out of five, plus anything it believes was invented, quoted word for word.

### Record it — and shout if it's bad

**Save the score** against the exact piece of work it graded, along with what the marking itself cost.

**Send it to the tracing dashboard**, so quality can be watched as a trend over time rather than read once and forgotten.

**Anything scoring two or below emails the operator straight away**, with the quoted problems attached. A quality drop should reach a person long before it could reach a customer.

## The test that proves the marker actually works

A grader that never catches anything is worthless — so it was tested with a trap.

Five false claims were deliberately planted in a copy of a real draft: a product that didn't exist, a price that was wrong, a promise nobody had made.

**It caught all five, quoted each one back, scored the draft 1 out of 5, and sent the alert.** Genuine work scores 5.0, 5.0 and 4.82.
